statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stands at 12 of 100 in the low band, thirteen points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 86 and confidence high at 88.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ slips to the lower edge of an unwidened overnight band at 29,078.75, down 0.19%, lifting tail only to 12, while a 4.944% ten-year, crude above $103 and 3.4% expected annual inflation keep stress extreme at 86 into the August consumer price report.
body:
The new evidence this hour is a change of position inside an unchanged range. NQ trades 29,078.75, down 56.50 points or 0.19%, against an overnight band of 29,061.75 to 29,171.50. An hour ago price sat at 29,127.25, near the middle of that band; it now sits in the lower third, about seventeen points above the low. The band itself has barely moved: the low has been extended by 0.75 points, or 0.003%, in five and a half hours since the 22:00 UTC reopen, and the high is untouched. A second independent quote source reports the same level and the same range, so the reading does not rest on a single feed.

That distinction is what keeps tail at 12 rather than higher. Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path, not direction. A slow fade toward the lower edge of a band that refuses to widen is the signature of a market still finding two-way interest at its extremes. The observable amplifiers are absent: there is no repeated extension after failed retracements, no shallow-pullback sequence, and no decisive rejection of the range. Price arriving near a session extreme is on its own a weak signal; extending from one is the meaningful one, and that has not happened. Tail therefore rises a single point from 11, and the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both instruments.

The backdrop is why stress ticks up to 86 and stays in the extreme band. The ten-year Treasury yield closed at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points on the session with an intraday high of 4.952%, its highest since 2023; the Federal Reserve's H.15 release puts the two-year at 4.43% and the ten-year at 4.83% as of 9 September, so the move is a fresh bear-steepening rather than a settled level. WTI trades above $103 and Brent above $105 after Saudi Arabia reported August output of 6.238 million barrels a day, its lowest since 1990, and after Iran declared attacks on ten ships including two U.S. vessels and eight oil tankers. VIX closed at 17.84, up 8.38%, elevated in change terms though still moderate in level. U.S. equities fell for a fourth consecutive session on 10 September, and reporting from that session puts market-implied odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase at the 16 September meeting near 69%.

Cross-asset context collected overnight is delayed, latest-session material and is used here only as confirmation. It shows semiconductors weak and broad, with six of seven names lower and a mean change near -3.0%, against megacaps that are internally split, five of eight lower but with one large-cap gaining more than 3%. Technology fell while communication services rose. That is conflicting breadth, and under the evidence rules conflicting breadth reduces directional conviction rather than mechanically raising tail. It supports the mixed dominant mode and the extreme stress reading at the same time.

The day's structure is known. The August consumer price report is released at 12:30 UTC, with consensus near 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, a level that already embeds much of the energy shock. The preliminary September Michigan sentiment and inflation-expectations survey follows at 14:00 UTC and the monthly budget statement at 18:00 UTC. The named danger window covers 12:30 to 14:30 UTC, where the conditional path peaks at tail 23, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold. An inflation surprise into a market already positioned for a hawkish outcome more reliably produces violent two-way repricing than the single sustained leg that tail measures, and the forward path is scored accordingly rather than escalated in advance.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 03:00 UTC on 10 September to 02:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 10 and holds a 9 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open, the only slot at the top of the watch band. Tail then decayed steadily as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the close and the reopen. The final six hours run 15, 14, 13, 12 and 11 as the overnight band settled. Stress never left the extreme band, ranging from 80 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence held between 84 and 89. Two published assessments fall inside the 12:00 UTC hour; the later one is recorded, consistent with the previous publication.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with roughly five and a half hours of observed post-reopen trade on 11 September and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC the same day. Conditional tail starts at 12, holds 12 through the late Asian hours and settles at an 11 floor across the thinnest pre-European hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European cash open it rebuilds gradually, 12 through 14, reaching 16 in the final full hour before the release as quoted depth thins and spreads widen. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, which stays inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold because an inflation surprise more reliably produces two-way repricing than a sustained no-retracement leg. The 13:00 UTC slot holds 22 across the cash open, where a post-event move is most often confirmed or rejected, and 14:00 UTC eases to 20 around the preliminary Michigan release. Tail then decays through the U.S. afternoon, 18, 16, 15 and 14, with a one-point rise to 15 into the penultimate cash hour for Friday weekend-risk hedging. From 21:00 UTC the series drops to a structural floor of 9 and then 7 with stress at 55, reflecting the absence of any tradable path in a closed market rather than an improving regime. Stress stays extreme from 85 to 90 through every open hour, and confidence runs 88 down to 83 at the event and 78 across the closure.
